Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

safe adjective

unharmed: safe and sound

also safe and sound, unharmed, unhurt, alive and well, get home safely, arrive safely, safe from danger

classical

Cic. Cat. 3.25: ut omnēs salvī cōnservārēminī (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 196: salvus et sānus
Traupman 66: well (in health)
Traupman 61: nōn salva vidēris, you don’t look well
Traupman 184: tē salvum et sānum domum rediisse, that you came home safe and sound
Traupman 405

salvus, salva, salvum

Declension on Wiktionary

safe, unharmed, all right

Saved, unharmed, well: the word behind the greetings salvē and salvus sīs, and Satin' salvē?, is everything all right? Often paired: salvus atque incolumis (Caes. B.C. 2.32).

Other words

  • incolumis, incolume — unhurt, intact, still alive

    also used · classical · Caes. B.G. 6.40.4: incolumēs ad ūnum omnēs in castra perveniunt (Lewis & Short); Catull. 9.6 · Declension on Wiktionary

    Unhurt and whole, of people, armies, ships, cities; the ablative is incolumī.

Examples

  • vīsam tē incolumem audiamque Hibērum narrantem loca, facta, nātiōnēs, ut mōs est tuus

    I’ll see you safe and sound and hear you tell of the places, deeds and peoples of Spain, as you always doCatull. 9.6–8

  • incolumēs ad ūnum omnēs in castra perveniunt

    they all reach the camp safe, to a manCaes. B.G. 6.40.4

  • tūtus ā perīculō

    safe from dangerTraupman 196

See also safe, is everything all right?, safe journey, hello.
